limitations: No live provider was contacted. Every check ran against loopback doubles: the OAuth authorization-server double, a client-credentials token endpoint and a loopback provider API, all through the real command service.

Evidence for the generic `catalog-http` adapter does not transfer to a host-registered entry: a pinned `catalog-<id>` adapter is labelled from entries naming its own id, so an entry nobody exercised reads `unverified`.
Entries whose auth mode cannot execute (for example OAuth 1.0a) are registered `catalog-only` and implement nothing.
workItems.notes: The provider-catalog adapter was delivered by the platform review stack, not by a swarm, and had no ledger, so the support matrix read `not-recorded` for it. This ledger records what the existing local suites already exercise. It adds no test and claims nothing live.

supportEvidence.notes: Authorization code, callback, proxy and refresh on expiry through the real command service against the loopback authorization-server double and a loopback provider API; origin and path confinement; no token in any output, view or error.
Client credentials, API key (header and query), Basic, bearer and no-credential modes end to end through the command service against loopback token and provider doubles.
A host-registered entry connects through its pinned catalog adapter (the same factory) after review, against loopback doubles; registration labels and the loopback opt-in.
Nango providers.yaml mapping into catalog entries and non-executable draft definitions.
Entry validation: HTTPS endpoints, template confinement, reserved parameters and bounds.

externalEffectsPerformed: None. No account was created, no provider contacted and no credential used; every double listens on 127.0.0.1.
